channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains ground after downbeat US industrial output
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades with a cautious tone as investors digest softer United States (US) industrial activity data while positioning for the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) interest rate decision due on Tuesday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rises on US-Iran de-escalation ahead of Fed decision
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5840 at the time of writing on Monday, up 0.17% on the day. The pair benefits from broad-based US Dollar (USD) weakness as markets welcome news of a framework agreement between the United States (US) and Iran aimed at ending the conflict between the two countries.

item.title: Gold climbs over 3% as US-Iran peace deal sends US Dollar, Oil prices lower
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) starts the week on a positive note, rising more than 3% after the United States (US) and Iran reached a framework agreement to end the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Global macro: Growth resilience and policy risks – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage emphasizes that, despite improved risk sentiment from geopolitical de-escalation, investors remain focused on central bank policy and global growth resilience.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains as US-Iran peace deal dents safe-haven demand for US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday as the Greenback's safe-haven demand fades following the United States and Iran's peace agreement aimed at ending the war in the Middle East. At the time of writing, USD/CHF trades around 0.7923, down 0.60% on the day.

item.title: US VP Vance: We expect Strait of Hormuz to be open toll-free long term
item.description: In an interview with CNBC on Monday, United States (US) Vice President JD Vance said that they expect the Strait of Hormuz to be "open toll-free in the long term," per Reuters.

item.title: Silver rallies as US Dollar slips on US-Iran framework, Fed decision looms
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $70.70 at the time of writing on Monday, up 3.94% on the day. The white metal is extending its rebound and benefiting from a backdrop marked by a weaker US Dollar (USD) and expectations surrounding the upcoming Federal Reserve (Fed) meeting.

item.title: Iran's Baghaei: Sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon part of agreement with US
item.description: Esmail Baghaei Hamaneh, the Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran, said on Monday that respecting sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon is a part of the interim agreement with the United States (US).

item.title: Brent: Prices retreat toward $80 on supply optimism – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman highlights that Oil prices have fallen back toward USD80 per barrel as markets anticipate normalized flows through the Strait of Hormuz after the US-Iran agreement.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Risk flows and policy focus – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage notes that the Japanese Yen is in focus as FX markets react to geopolitical de-escalation and shifting risk sentiment. The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz has supported risk assets, but investors remain attentive to policy divergence involving JPY, KRW and USD.

item.title: Canadian Dollar hovers near seven-month lows as lower Oil prices offset risk appetite
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is trading without a clear bias against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday.

item.title: Global markets: Oil, bonds and equities react to conflict – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank reviews performance of Oil, bonds, European equities and precious metals from late February to last Friday during the conflict. The bank notes Oil and AI-related trades surged, while bonds, most European equities and precious metals fell.

item.title: United States Dollar: Policy divergence and risk sentiment – BNY
item.description: According to BNY’s Bob Savage, the Dollar is trading within a broader risk-on environment after the U.S.-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz eased energy supply concerns. FX markets are highly sensitive to policy divergence, with USD trends reassessed alongside JPY and KRW.

item.title: SNB to keep interest rates at 0% on June 18 and for rest of year – Reuters poll
item.description: According to the June 11-15 Reuters poll, all 35 economists predicted that the Swiss National Bank (SNB) would keep its policy rate at 0% this week. 28 economists ​who responded with forecasts until the end of 2026 saw rates staying at 0% the entire year.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Short positioning elevated into BoJ hike – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman observes that the Japanese Yen has not benefited from lower energy prices, with USD/JPY still above 160.00 ahead of the BoJ meeting.

item.title: ECB’s Kazimir: Stresses on frontloading interest rate hikes despite US-Iran peace deal
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council member and Governor of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) Peter Kazimir seems to be joining his peers in highlighting the need for further monetary policy adjustments on the upside despite the United States (US) and Iran reaching a peace framework.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Range trading outlook – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) discusses USD/CAD, noting the pair has been consolidating and may remain range-bound. The bank highlights that recent moves reflect shifting expectations for Federal Reserve and Bank of Canada policy.

item.title: Gold advances as US-Iran framework deal, weaker Dollar support rebound
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades around $4,340 at the time of writing on Monday, up 2.86% on the day and extending the rebound that began on Thursday from the $4,024 area.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Holds near 0.7090 with bullish pressure mounting
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trims previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as markets ponder the peace agreement between the US and Iran, ahead of a central bank-busy week.

item.title: Brent: Lower prices with key supports – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux and colleagues note Brent has dropped sharply after the US–Iran MoU and reopening prospects for the Strait of Hormuz, with prices down 35% from April peaks but still above pre-war levels.

item.title: The BoJ is about to hike: Why the Japanese Yen is still pinned near 160.00
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to trade firmly around the psychologically crucial 160.00 level against the US Dollar.

item.title: Euro: Gradual upside path outlined – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s FX Strategy team at RaboResearch Global Economics & Markets discusses how the Dollar initially benefited from safe haven flows during the Iran war, but has since softened as a ceasefire memorandum eased market tensions and tempered Fed hike expectations.

item.title: Global Macro: Hawkish pivot shapes risk landscape – HSBC
item.description: HSBC Asset Management’s Investment Weekly highlights how higher Oil prices, China’s export surge and US AI investment are reshaping the global macro backdrop.

item.title: Euro holds gains as risk appetite offsets downbeat Eurozone data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) maintains its positive tone against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, with the EUR/USD pair trading near 10-day highs above 1.1600.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Yen underperforms amid BoJ rate outlook uncertainty
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) trades lower against its major currency peers during the European trading session on Monday, while the USD/JPY pair is marginally lower at around 160.15 after recovering its early losses.

item.title: Australian Dollar advances as US-Iran framework boosts risk appetite ahead of RBA decision
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7070 at the time of writing on Monday, up 0.35% on the day, benefiting from renewed risk appetite after the United States (US) and Iran announced a framework agreement aimed at ending their conflict.

item.title: Indian Rupee holds strength on US-Iran deal finalization
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades strongly against the US Dollar (USD) in India's afternoon trading hours on Monday. The USD/INR pair plunges to near 94.60 as oil prices have nosedived, following the announcement that the United States (US) and Iran have reached a permanent peace deal.

item.title: US Dollar: Weaker path after US-Iran deal – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that the US Dollar has extended losses after the US and Iran reached an interim agreement to end conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank caution weighs on Krona – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman (BBH) expects the Riksbank to keep its policy rate at 1.75% for a sixth consecutive meeting and to lean against market pricing for a 25 bps hike by year-end.

item.title: British Pound: BoE hikes and politics cap Pound – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman expects the Bank of England to hold at 3.75% with a 7–2 vote and sees the first fully priced 25 bps hike in November.
